literal: To the bright-foreheaded one, oh, broke indeed, in the battlefield, even enemies will fear, my strength.
translation: Alas! My strength and valour, which even the fiercest enemies on the battlefield would fear, has been completely shattered by this bright-foreheaded maiden.
modern: போர்க்களத்தில் பகைவர்களும் அஞ்சுகின்ற என்னுடைய வலிமையானது, இந்த ஒளிபொருந்திய நெற்றியை உடையவளுக்கு முன்னால், ஐயோ! உடைந்துபோனதே!
explanation: The hero laments the sudden loss of his legendary strength in the presence of the heroine. He is a mighty warrior whose valour (pīṭu) strikes terror even in his enemies (naṇṇārum) on the battlefield (ñāṭpiṉuḷ). Yet, confronted by the beauty of this woman with a bright forehead (oṇṇutaṟku), his strength has completely shattered (uṭaintatē). The exclamation 'ōo' emphasizes his astonishment and vulnerability at being defeated not by weapons, but by love.
